This community has a pattern of throwing fits and review bombing this game over ANYTHING (the PS+ thing is fair I think thats bs) like this modding thing, if this was a single player I would get the hate but I've had ALOT of encounters where modders/hackers have ruined rounds for me and others.

 Arrowhead simply do not want that happening and I dont get were throwing a fit over it for. "But my cosmetic mods" your playing as fucking master chief or a over sexualized version of a helldiver or bug dude. And I dont understand the mods that changes the difficulty or adds new missions, I like the idea new mission I would just rather wait for AH to add them into the game themselves (this is just a preference though).  

Arrow Head could make better choices for this games future Im not denying it (I have my fair share of things to say about it) but review bombing the game over Arrow Head wanting to get rid of hackers is crazy to me. 

My overall point with this is that when it comes to steam reviews this is just the most inconsistent game because the review bombing issue just sucks in this community and when it comes to something like modding I think its just a bad reason to review bomb, we shouldn't really be review bombing a LIVE service game for the people who made it wanting to to be played as made. 

Helldivers 2 has its issues ALOT actually (constant rag dolling, statergem bouncing, reinforcement drifting and more) but we go crazy over a game studio wanting for their game to be played as intended is what makes us lash out really?

If you came for a actual review I find the game fun can be irritating at times and I really hate how Arrow Head neglects the stealth part of this game (I am a stealth diver) and I wish they did more with stealth like in base operations en such.

这个游戏我可以给70分
先说好的方面：这游戏真的很好玩
合作射击的教科书。四人小队各司其职，防空、反坦克和清杂、解密分工明确，每一局打起来都有战术配合的满足感。支援武器呼叫、队友倒地互救、撤离倒计时前的绝境翻盘，以及队友的娱乐性互坑和搞事情——这些时刻带来的快乐是纯粹的。
射击手感顶级。枪械后坐力、命中反馈、爆炸效果打磨的非常到位，就感觉像是亲手拿着枪械去战斗。打虫子的爆浆感、打机器人的爆炸爽感、打光能者的打击反馈感至今很难能找出第二款游戏。
真正的战斗氛围。 空袭会误伤队友、炮击支援不分敌我，"民主的炮弹不民主"这种混乱感反而构成了游戏独特的魅力。再加上官方持续的剧情推进和玩家的集体"战役参与感"和“战役史诗感，这是别的游戏给不了的体验。
内容更新勤快。自发售以来新武器、新敌人、新任务类型基本没断过，制作组对社区反馈的响应速度也算业界良心。
再说不足：服务器是最大败笔！！！
连接质量差强人意。 这是我最想吐槽的点：高峰时段卡顿明显，联机过程中掉线时有发生。好不容易打到撤离环节突然掉线，一局的心血全白费，挫败感极强！！！
掉线惩罚机制不合理。明明不是你的网络问题，重连回来后进度和奖励却可能丢失，玩家却要为服务器的锅买单，这一点真的很伤积极性，此时挫败感是顶级的！！！
如果能容忍掉线带来的偶发血压飙升，这是一款值得入手的顶级合作射击游戏。内容量、手感、氛围都在线，打折时更是闭眼入。
扣的30分，全扣给服务器！管理式民主需要你，但请先把服务器修好。

Helldivers 2 — это настоящий шедевр в жанре шутеров от первого лица! 🎮💥 Игра поражает своей эпичностью и масштабностью: каждый шаг в этом мире наполнен адреналином и драйвом.
Потрясающая графика и детализированный дизайн уровней создают ощущение полного погружения в постапокалиптический мир, где каждое сражение — это настоящее зрелище. 
Особенно впечатляет кооперативный режим: объединяться с друзьями и сражаться против инопланетных захватчиков — это не просто весело, а по-настоящему захватывающе! 🤝
Геймплей предлагает множество вариантов развития персонажа и тактик ведения боя, что делает каждую миссию уникальной и непредсказуемой. 
Helldivers 2 — это именно та игра, которая заставляет забыть о реальности и погрузиться в мир бесконечных сражений и побед. Обязательно рекомендую всем фанатам жанра и любителям захватывающих приключений! 🚀🔥
P.S. Держитесь крепче за свои джойстики, эта игра не отпустит вас!  Игроков с консолями очень- очень много :)

FOR PLAYERS CRASHING ON STARTUP (after anticheat update) - [strike]try removing armory crate (asus) or RGB controller programs and see if that's the problem, then report.[/strike]  EDIT: SO, turns out this may not be the issue, the error came back.  After rebooting, it would launch.  Then it came back again, another reboot then can launch again.  Seems like quite the blunder how this problem was missed when its affecting so many people.

Summary of my positives:
An absolute blast of a game, especially with friends.  It has great effects, punchy sounds and good feel on the weapons.  They've updated them a lot and tried to make them all fun to use.  It scratches a lot of itches that are lacking in other games.  They keep adding more stuff to the game that keeps me coming back for new toys to play with.  The 3 factions make it so that you get to devise a new set of gear that works for your playstyle and each new warbonds brings new ways to tweak your playstyle or toys that go along with that playstyle.

My biggest complaints:
The initial push for Sony to force account creation and linking, and then making it so that other countries couldn't play it after they had bought it.
That there needs to be new types of missions added regularly along with warbonds.  I haven't had but a couple problems that everyone is complaining about, but fixed.
There has been on occasion situations or updates that have added crashes or problems loading.  For me its been a few times.

REGARDING THE RECENT ANTICHEAT:  It has caused problems, even for me initially.  For my problem to launch the game after the update, which came 2 days after the update, was an error I could not pin down initially, [strike]but it turned out to be my ASUS armory crate programs, likely to be the RGB controller itself, but I'm unsure specifically which of the armory crate programs caused it.  I tried everything recommended, even reinstalling the game, and nothing worked until i removed armory crate software.  Now, I don't like that i have to remove legitimate software to play the game and that needs to be addressed, but perhaps this will help someone.[/strike]

On the side of cheating in a PVE games.  Fair play is fair play, regardless of PVE or PVP.  HOWEVER, i do realize that the impact is smaller on a massive factor in PVE vs PVP, but it does not change the fact that cheating is cheating.  Only on a few occasions have I been impacted by cheaters that was bad enough that I and others noticed.  The most egregious cheat created an aura of damage from one player resulting in the highest team damage I've ever seen in this game.  A number that couldn't even be achieved if he had just dropped bombs on us the entire mission.  It's a problem because the cheat kept setting off hellbombs killing his teammates, constantly draining our life so we used up all our stims and would die when encountering enemies with additional damage occurring and no stims to heal.  This is quite annoying.  Also, cheating reporting is non existent.  The option is there but they only recommend blocking to handle cheating.  This prevents you from encountering the player again in matchmaking and that, ultimately is fine I guess.  I strongly dislike cheaters in ANY team environment.  Solo, fine, do whatever you want.  But the current decision to switch anti cheat software has caused more headaches and I don't know if that was worthwhile from a players perspective.

If I had to review this game, for the moment, not good. My reason is that for some stupid the pc I use has all the requirements for this game, but it is a touch screen as well. I think that Helldivers 2 thinks that my pc is a mobile device or something incompatible. I'm unable to pass the intro cutscene without the game either crashing or kicking me out from even looking at settings. So I dislike that part. On the other hand, from what I have seen and listened to, it is a really fun and "nice" game that gives a damn good reason to release anger.

Do I recommend this game? Yes. Do I wish that Arrowhead would focus on fixing issues for once? Also yes. This game easily one of my favorites. Awesome gameplay, great with friends, absolutely hilarious at times. But this game comes with many issues. Being a Roblox kid, I've learned to cope with the most diabolical bugs imaginable and least balanced games ever. However, even I have noticed some pretty big ones in Helldivers 2. For example, wretches and fleshmobs sometimes clip through walls, players can rarely get stuck in terrain, as well as a few others. But these bugs don't make the game bad. It is still a perfectly fun game and is worth the money. Could the game be better? Sure. Update quality and progression still need some work. Let's start with the negatives, from someone who plays [i]a lot[/i] of PvE games and horde shooters:
[list]
    [*]If you're strictly in the market for hyper-fast, skill-indexed, aim-intensive experiences built around animation canceling and the like, you'll probably want to look elsewhere.  This game has a lot of built-in clunkiness like aim-sway (e.g. your gun does not snap to aim, there's a delay on where you point your mouse vs. when the thing moves and it gets better or worse with certain weapons based on your loadout.  Its base design dissuades trying to play it like a reflex-heavy shooter and it will absolutely frustrate you from time to time, as it also does to myself.
    [*]If you are a fan of melee combat in dedicated shooters, do not play this game.  Find something else.
    [*]The general experience, especially in the higher difficulties, can be [i]wildly[/i] inconsistent.  You can have a difficulty 10 group of randos that completely roflstomp missions back-to-front multiple times in a row, and then SOS-drop into a difficulty 7 game that is a wall-to-wall misery simulator where players fail to get anything done except call in infinite reinforcements.  The 8-10 difficulty settings kinda blend together on the general experience except that Diff 10 games have super-duper sized fortresses you have to deal with.
    [*]Out of any other horde game I've played in recent memory, Helldivers 2 has the [i]whiniest[/i], most entitled general playerbase on public forums and the like.  If you went entirely by discussion boards you'd be convinced that the developers working on this game caught lightning in a bottle purely to lord over their playerbase out of distilled spite.  Rarely do I encounter awful people in this game proper--usually by the time you hit Diff 9/10 players have that general air of "chill via competence," for lack of a better term--but avoid any sort of discussion boards like the plague.  More squealers than a pig farm.
    [*]On that note, if you are allergic to devs nerfing cheese and believe "no nerf only buff" is a sound design philosophy, do not play this game, lest you become one of the aforementioned squealers somehow deeply invested in a game you clearly do not enjoy.
[/list] 

That said, as horde shooters go, it's still pretty fun.  If you can get past the more mil-sim-ish elements of the game and the learning curve that comes with all the knowledge checks, there's a lot of entertainment to be had in the general mayhem you can unleash.

As of the time of writing there's three general factions: Terminids (mostly hordes that rush you in melee with pure numbers), Automatons (slow but armored tanks with guns), and Illuminates (something in between the former two enemy types).  You're not obligated to play along with the game's Major Orders or story--effectively they are glorified weeklies that try to force players out of comfort zones--but you can if you want, and I encourage you to do so in order to get the most experience at handling all the enemy factions and sub-factions.
Some factions obviously encourage you to lean on different weapons than others.  For example, Bugs are chaff-heavy and die to anti-swarm measures but hard punish methodical aim-based players, while Bots are basically the opposite and encourage marksmanship and use of cover, smokes, etc. in gunfights.  You are free to take whatever pleases you and, if you get comfortable with the powerful yet unwieldy tools the game offers, can become quite a wizard at dealing with whatever the game throws your way.

Even weapons widely derided as subpar or bad can be wielded to frightening effect, if you're willing to put the work in.  That, really, is where most of the fun with this game lies: mixing and matching your loadouts where you're not an obvious millstone on your squad, but good enough to get away with a lot that you'd think you can't.  Once you drop into failing games and turn things around armed with nothing but a humble sniper rifle, smoke grenades, and a burning desire for decommissioning computers on legs, you'll get it.

Deixe-me compartilhar uma história que certamente irá tocar seu coração. Aos 57 anos, sou um pai solteiro, e minha maior prioridade sempre foi criar meu filho de 14 anos.

Recentemente, meu filho recebeu Helldivers 2 de presente de seu tio. Em apenas uma semana, já havia acumulado 24 horas espalhando a democracia pela galáxia. Preocupado com o tempo que passávamos separados, decidi comprar o jogo na Steam para que pudéssemos jogar juntos.

Foi a melhor decisão da minha vida.

Na primeira missão, não fazia ideia do que estava fazendo. Acidentalmente, lancei um ataque orbital sobre meu próprio filho, eliminando toda a nossa equipe. Em vez de ficar bravo, ele começou a rir como eu não o via rir há anos.

Naquela noite, passamos horas lutando contra insetos gigantes, fugindo de robôs assassinos e morrendo repetidamente pela liberdade.

Desde a trágica perda de minha esposa, fazia muito tempo que não me sentia tão próximo do meu filho. Hoje, não somos apenas pai e filho. Somos irmãos de armas, soldados da Superterra, unidos por um propósito maior.

Este jogo não apenas fortaleceu nossa relação, mas também me ensinou que a verdadeira felicidade está nas pequenas coisas: uma família, uma risada e uma bomba de 500 kg caindo sobre nossos inimigos.

Nota: 10/10. Pela democracia. Pela liberdade. Pela Superterra.

Edit: Meu filho acabou de me chamar para mais uma missão. Não posso deixá-lo esperando. A democracia não se espalha sozinha.

I genuinely love Helldivers 2. When this game is firing on all cylinders, there really isn’t much else like it. The ridiculous moments, the chaos when everything goes wrong, pulling off a mission that should have been a complete disaster, and just screwing around with friends while somehow still getting the job done. That is what keeps me coming back.

Is it perfect? Absolutely not. There have been balance decisions I haven’t agreed with, bugs that have hung around longer than they should, and times where it feels like the developers are fighting the community instead of listening to it. But none of that changes the fact that underneath those problems is a genuinely great game.

My biggest issue right now is the recent anti-cheat change.

I understand wanting to stop actual cheating. Nobody wants somebody coming into their game and ruining the experience. That's completely reasonable. But there is a huge difference between stopping people who cheat and effectively kneecapping the modding community in the process.

The move to Easy Anti-Cheat has broken a lot of mods, and even some non-malicious cosmetic mods may need to be reworked by their creators. That's a real problem because the modding community isn't the enemy here. They're some of the most dedicated people playing this game.

A healthy modding community helps keep a PC game alive. They create cosmetics, quality-of-life improvements, fixes, customization and reasons for longtime players to keep coming back. In some cases, players have been using mods specifically to address frustrations with the base game that haven't been resolved yet.

And honestly, I think that's the part Arrowhead needs to recognize.

Go after the people cheating. Go after mods that negatively affect other players or manipulate the Galactic War. I have absolutely no problem with that. But please don't burn down the house just to kill a few bugs inside it.

Helldivers 2 has something special, and I don't want to see it lose one of the communities helping keep that something special alive.

I still recommend the game. I still have a ridiculous amount of fun playing it. This isn't coming from somebody who hates Helldivers 2. It's coming from somebody who likes it enough to be disappointed when I think it's heading in the wrong direction.
